Backgrounds as math

Yes — and gradients already are the linear algebra. A radial-gradient evaluates the norm ‖p − c‖ at every pixel; linear-gradient evaluates the projection p · n; conic-gradient evaluates atan2(p − c). Blend modes are the operators that combine those fields: multiply is a·b, difference is |a − b|. SVG filters add the rest — a matrix on colour, a convolution kernel, and a vector field on coordinates.

The one that solves your problem is the last. Noise makes a page busy because it adds high-frequency energy, and a white ground shows that energy first — which is exactly what you saw. Displacement adds none: it moves samples of a field that was already smooth. So a warped gradient is differentiable everywhere and irregular in shape at the same time. Compare 7 against 8 below, then flip to Kindled and compare them again.

‖p − c‖ A distance field. radial-gradient is the L2 norm from a point, mapped through the colour stops. Cost nil · both worlds fine
p · n A projection onto a normal. linear-gradient is a dot product, which is why its iso-lines are always parallel and always straight. Cost nil · reads as lighting
atan2(p − c) An angle field. conic-gradient sweeps the argument, so it makes rays rather than rings — useful for a shaft, wrong for dirt. Cost nil · too directional
|f₁ − f₂| − f₃ Superposition. Three plane waves at unrelated angles and periods, subtracted by background-blend-mode: difference. Real interference, and a textbook moiré. Cost nil · far too busy
M · rgba feColorMatrix is a literal 5×4 linear map on the colour vector. Here it routes alpha into the colour channels, which is how the stain filter turns luminance into opacity. Cost low · a tool, not a texture
K ∗ f feConvolveMatrix, a 3×3 kernel whose weights sum to zero. Flat areas cancel and only the gradient survives, so a soft blob comes out looking carved. Cost medium · stone, not soot
p ↦ p + s·F(p) The recommendation. A smooth radial gradient displaced by a low-frequency vector field. Irregular iso-lines, zero added high-frequency energy, no tile and therefore no seam. Cost medium · calm in both worlds
F(p) The same Perlin basis used directly instead of as a displacement. This is the busy one, and it is busiest on white. Cost medium · the thing you rejected
◆

Program Analysis

Symbolic Execution

02 June 2026 · Nine minutes

Symbolic execution is a means of analyzing a program to determine what inputs cause each part of it to execute. Instead of running the code on real values, an interpreter walks it while holding every input as a symbol.

It arrives at expressions written in terms of those symbols, and at constraints for the outcome of each conditional branch. Where concrete execution answers what a program does with 5, symbolic execution answers what it would take to reach a place at all.

A worked example

int f() {
  y = read();
  z = y * 2;
  if (z == 12) fail();
  else printf("OK");
}

During symbolic execution the program reads a symbol, λ, and the branch condition becomes the constraint λ * 2 == 12. Execution forks, and a solver later returns 6 to reach fail().

Limitations

Merge states that differ only in irrelevant ways and you accept weaker constraints. Bound the loops and you accept incompleteness past the bound. Prioritize paths heuristically and the interesting one may be starved.

Engines worth reading next: KLEE and angr.

What it costs to ship

<!-- once, anywhere in the document -->
<filter id="warp" color-interpolation-filters="sRGB">
  <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.0022"
                numOctaves="2" seed="11" result="F"/>
  <feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" in2="F" scale="420"
                     xChannelSelector="R" yChannelSelector="G"/>
</filter>

/* the layer. inset is negative so the warp cannot pull
   transparent pixels in from outside the element. */
.air {
  position: fixed;
  inset: -20%;
  z-index: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  background: radial-gradient(110% 80% at 50% 16%,
                transparent 26%, var(--vignette) 100%);
  filter: url(#warp);
}

Three honest caveats. The filter rasterizes once per resize, so inset: -20% on a full-window layer is real work on a phone — measure before shipping it. scale is in pixels, so it does not respond to viewport size; the warp looks stronger on a small screen. And Safari has historically been the weakest at feDisplacementMap on large surfaces, so this is the one technique on the page worth testing on a real device rather than trusting.

What CSS still cannot do. There is no loop, so a sum over N terms has to be written out N times — variation 4 above is three lines because three was as far as it was worth going by hand. calc() has sin(), cos(), pow(), sqrt() and hypot() since 2023, but they compute lengths and angles for properties, not values per pixel. Genuine per-pixel programs need the Houdini Paint API, which after seven years is still Chromium-only — so it is a progressive enhancement at best, never the thing the page depends on.
